gap._description: Swift's modern surface is largely handled: actors/structs/enums/extensions (class_declaration + anonymous keyword token), protocols + associated types, operators, subscripts, optional binding, error handling, macros, conditional compilation, and per-symbol cyclomatic complexity. Remaining gaps are exotic macro/type forms the pinned grammar parses but the analyzer does not yet emit as symbols.

gaps.node_type: operator_declaration, custom_operator, precedence_group_declaration, precedence_group_attributes, precedence_group_attribute, deprecated_operator_declaration_body
gaps.missing: custom operator + precedence-group declarations as symbols (operator overloads on types ARE handled; file-scope operator/precedence declarations are not)
generic packs and fully-open ranges as distinct symbols

gaps.node_type: key_path_expression, key_path_string_expression, selector_expression, constructor_expression, constructor_suffix, metatype, opaque_type, existential_type

decisions.question: The pinned grammar (alex-pinkus style) has ONE class_declaration node for class/struct/actor/enum/extension — the kind is decided by the anonymous keyword token.
decisions.resolution: The analyzer reads the anonymous keyword token (class/struct/enum/extension/actor) to pick the kind — never source-text scanning. Only CLASS can have a superclass: its FIRST base is extends ONLY when that base is a class. A first-base protocol is still an adoption (implements). Kind resolution: an in-file pre-pass records declared protocol/class names, and the cross-file companion (context.typeKinds, corpus protocol set) covers other files; unknown externals follow the deterministic Swift rule (first base = superclass extends). Structs and actors have NO superclass — every base is implements.

decisions.question: Operator overloads (`static func + (l:r:)`) have no simple_identifier name — the name is the anonymous operator token after `func`.
decisions.resolution: Emitted as method symbols named `operator +` / `operator ==` / `operator []` (the dart #265 operator-signature convention); their bodies' calls/instantiates attach to the operator method.

decisions.question: Subscript READS (`entries[key]`) parse as call_expression with a `[key]` call_suffix — indistinguishable from a function call by node type alone.
decisions.resolution: A call_suffix whose value_arguments open with `[` is a property read — NO calls edge (family property-read precedent). `defer { }` also parses as a call_expression; it is filtered as a keyword construct, never a calls edge.

decisions.question: Swift inits have no distinct name; deinit and subscripts are not first-class symbols.
decisions.resolution: init -> constructor named "constructor" (Java/C# family convention); deinit and subscript are NOT symbols (ObjC dealloc / C# indexer precedent) but their bodies' calls still emit with the enclosing type as source.

decisions.question: `self.x` member READS vs `self.method()` CALLS both parse as navigation_expression.
decisions.resolution: A navigation_expression that is the callee of a call_expression is a CALL (calls edge to leaf); otherwise with a self receiver it is a member read (uses edge, source = enclosing METHOD, target = leaf). M49 W15 #814: the source was the enclosing TYPE until the family-wide ruling converged on method-source (java/swift/javascript moved; python/dart/cpp already agreed); a class-level read has no method and falls back to the type.

decisions.question: Is where_clause a real, fixture-coverable shape in the pinned grammar?
decisions.resolution: No. Probe-verified 2026-09-02: generic `where T: Equatable` clauses parse as type_constraints (with where_keyword + type_constraint children); no Swift source produces a where_clause node. The grammar declares it but it is unreachable. Reclassified from handled_verified per the F6 fixture-coverage gate (M14.0.F6).

decisions.question: The Pass-3 first-parent fallback emitted its GUESS at confidence 1.0 with evidenceClass 'structural' — indistinguishable from a verified override in thresholded analysis. What is the correct tier contract?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): verified overrides (in-file Pass-1) stay @1.0/structural; the Pass-3 first-parent guess is @0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and tier 'inferred' (classifyEvidenceTier <0.9 branch) — matching java/groovy's documented Pass-3 contract and staying below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold. The guess may target a parent that never declares the method; claiming structural hid the evidence gap. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-SWIFT, the swift/external-override fixture + confidence pins, and 6 family regression mutants.

decisions.question: Protocol inheritance (`protocol A: B, C`) emitted NO edge — a comment claimed ObjC `@protocol A <NSObject>` precedent, but the managed-OO family materializes interface extends (csharp `interface IX : IA` -> extends, java `interface IX extends IA` -> extends, objc `@protocol B <A>` -> extends). Probe-verified 2026-09 on swift-nio: 46 protocol-inheritance sites, both sides silent.
decisions.resolution: protocol inheritance now emits extends per parent (weight 1). AnyObject/Any inheritance_specifiers are CLASS-CONSTRAINT markers, not protocol parents — probe-verified (`protocol P: AnyObject, B` in swift-nio parses AnyObject as an inheritance_specifier) — excluded from the extends set.

decisions.question: Extension conformances (`extension Circle: Equatable`) emitted NOTHING — base extraction was skipped for the Extension kind. Swift forbids redundant conformances, so every extension base is an ADDITIONAL adoption. Corpus: 380 sites in swift-nio (554 files). csharp partial-class conformance is the managed-OO analog and IS materialized.
decisions.resolution: extension bases now emit implements (weight 0.9) sourced from the extension symbol (named after the extended type). Extensions cannot add a superclass, so no extends is ever possible.

decisions.question: Enum bases were skipped entirely AND the first base was always recorded as rawType metadata — so `enum Result: Error` minted bogus rawType=Error payload (Error is a conformance) and no conformance edges ever emitted. Corpus: 181 enums carry bases; ~93% first-slot are protocols (Sendable 76 / Error 46 / Hashable 22 / Equatable 17 / String 7 / Int 5 / UInt8 1).
decisions.resolution: only a stdlib-named first base (String/Character/Int8-64/UInt8-64/Float/Double/CGFloat) is the raw value (meta.rawType, no edge); every other base is a protocol conformance -> implements (weight 0.9). Mirrors dart DARTD15 (enhanced-enum conformances). Custom RawRepresentable raw types in first slot are unresolvable statically; the stdlib gate is the deterministic rule (accepted boundary).

decisions.question: Bare capitalized calls emit instantiates (Swift construction syntax), but two non-type families fabricate edges: XCTest assertion FUNCTIONS (XCTAssertEqual/XCTFail/... — the one capitalized free-function family in Swift; 8,226 of 13,966 capitalized bare calls = 59% in the swift-nio census) and stdlib fixed-width numerics (UInt64/Int64/UInt8 — 1,105 stdlib constructions — while Int/Double/String were already in BUILTIN_BARE_CALLS, an inconsistency). Both sides colluded (F5-blind).
decisions.resolution: XCT-prefixed bare callees are filtered (no edge — they are not types, matching BuiltinsAreFiltered); fixed-width stdlib numerics (UInt/UInt8-64/Int8-64) joined BUILTIN_BARE_CALLS. Genuine external type construction (DispatchQueue etc, undeclared in corpus) still emits instantiates. Oracle mirrored exactly.

decisions.question: Subscript access of a SELF container (`self.storage[k]`, `self.storage[k] = v`) emitted NO uses — the write/call gates treated the subscript base as an assignment LHS / method-call callee. But a subscript access is a property READ of the container, not a write to it and not a method invocation. Family precedent probe-verified 2026-09 on the same shapes: php emits `uses read->items` AND `uses write->items`, objc emits both too. 62 subscript self-container accesses in the 200-file swift-nio census (49 reads, 13 writes) — all silently dropped, both sides (differential-invisible).
decisions.resolution: Subscript base navigations with a self receiver now emit uses (container read); the method-call callee suppression is scoped to NON-subscript call_expression parents only. A pure field write (`self.count = 0`) stays gated by the SCD1 write gate (probe-verified: it never reaches this gate — its parent is the assignment LHS wrapper). Subscript-write bases are container reads, matching php/objc. Mirror in deriveSwiftEdges. Gated by fixture swift/master-review-w2-regressions (expectUses Cache->storage/key, forbid uses Cache->count) + mutant swift/drop-container-subscript-uses + swift/re-add-field-write-uses.

decisions.question: Multi-binding declarations (`var a = 1, b = 2`, top-level `let g1 = 1, g2 = 2`) symbolized only the FIRST binding — the declaration carries one sibling `pattern` child PER binding in the pinned grammar (probe-verified 2026-09), and handleVariable read only findChildByType(pattern). 0 corpus sites in the 200-file swift-nio census but a real completeness hole: every additional property/variable was silently dropped.
decisions.resolution: handleVariable now iterates ALL sibling pattern children and creates one symbol per binding (kind property/variable by scope). Locals remain non-symbols by contract (the handler early-returns for non-type parents). Gated by fixture swift/master-review-w2-regressions (expectSymbols second/gTop2) + mutant swift/drop-second-binding-symbol.

decisions.question: Dotted qualified type names were resolved to the FIRST segment everywhere. `extension Outer2.Inner2` minted an extension symbol named Outer2 — colliding with the container struct's symbol id and mis-attributing every extension member to the container (97 dotted extension targets in the 200-file swift-nio census, mostly nested-type extensions like WebSocketFrame._Storage / NIOBSDSocket.AddressFamily). Dotted inheritance bases fabricated edges to the module/container name: `class Sub2: Foundation.URLSession` emitted extends Sub2->Foundation, `struct M2: SharedMod.Proto` emitted implements M2->SharedMod (6 dotted bases in the census).
decisions.resolution: A user_type holds its dotted segments as sibling type_identifier children in source order (probe-verified), so the leaf is the LAST type_identifier — consistent with the family's leaf-target convention everywhere else. Extension targets now name the leaf (Inner2); extractBaseName now returns the leaf (URLSession/Proto). Oracle baseName mirrored. Gated by fixture swift/master-review-w2-regressions (expects extends NetSession->URLSession, implements M2->Proto, extension symbol Inner2; forbids contains Outer2->operator ==, extends NetSession->Foundation, implements M2->SharedMod) + mutants swift/first-segment-dotted-base + swift/first-segment-extension-name.

decisions.question: OO family closure #613 family sweep (shared-blind-spot): bare capitalized calls emit instantiates — but the M12.21 `target.length > 1` carve-out mislabels single-letter constructions. Is length meaningful for the construction rule?
decisions.resolution: No — Swift naming reserves single capital letters for types (never free functions), so `E()` where `struct E: Error` is construction (instantiates ONLY). The carve-out had no rationale and was shared by analyzer + oracle (F5-blind): 15 sites in swift-nio corpus tests all degraded to calls. Guard removed on both sides; single-letter-construction fixture + swift/single-letter-as-calls mutant pin it.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: cross-type member reads (`store.items.count`, `a.b.c` links, `C.shared`, `o.items[k]`) invisible on both sides — self-uses and bare-uses both missed them (dart DT-F / objc OC-E / php PHP-A parity).
decisions.resolution: Suffix members read unless callee (last suffix of a non-subscript func-nav), self-chained (handleSelfUse owns), LHS-span writes (SCD1), implicit-dot roots, or self/Self/$0. Shares emittedUses (first metadata wins). Confidence 0.9. Gated by fixture swift/member-value-reads + mutants swift/drop-member-read-uses, swift/emit-member-write-as-uses.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: `Result.success(1)` dangled as calls->success (no such method; dart DT-A disease) while bare `Suit()` correctly instantiated.
decisions.resolution: Candidates (capitalized direct receiver + leaf) recorded in-call, resolved post-walk against declared enum cases (in-file exactness; static factories and cross-file/Self heads stay calls). Dangling leaf dropped, instantiates emitted. Oracle mirrors with its own prescan (enums parse as class_declaration + enum token, caught by probe). Gated by fixture + mutants swift/enum-ctor-leaf-call, swift/static-factory-instantiates.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: `\.name`, `\C.name`, `o[keyPath: \.slot]` — key-path members invisible on both sides (pervasive in SwiftUI: ForEach id, bindings).
decisions.resolution: Key-path suffix members always read (even the set-through form reads WHICH member). self/Self skipped. Gated by fixture (moved from silent list to handled).

decisions.question: Ultimate review: `type(of: x)` emitted calls->type — a stdlib free function like print/assert, never user code.
decisions.resolution: Added to BUILTIN_BARE_CALLS + oracle SWIFT_BUILTINS. Member positions unaffected. Gated by fixture forbid + mutant swift/type-call-restored.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: `$count` (projected @State value) missed the member table (`count` declared, `$count` read) — silent on both sides. `$0` shorthands must stay silent.
decisions.resolution: Bare-uses + oracle mirror strip leading $ (all-digit rests skipped) for lookup AND target. Gated by fixture + mutant swift/projected-read-dropped.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: `#assert(x)` freestanding macros error-recover (no edges either side); `a + b` silent; closure implicit captures silent (locals); metatypes (`is`/`as`/`C.self`) silent.
decisions.resolution: Macros are a pinned-grammar boundary (definitions patterned, use-sites blind — corpora unaffected). Operators are arithmetic dispatch. Implicit captures are locals by design (explicit structural captures differ per language: php use-lists emit, Swift has none). Metatypes are types, not values. All consistent both sides.

decisions.question: Ultimate review: is `"hello \(name)"` covered? Dart/PHP needed blankets.
decisions.resolution: Already covered by composition: `\(o.prop)` members via SW-A, bare members via handleBareUses (wrappers fixture proves uses[V->count] from Text), locals silent by design. No separate rule; pinned indirectly.

decisions.question: Second review: `super.init(x)`, `self.init(0)` emitted calls->init (dangling — constructors are literally `constructor`) or nothing — every initializer delegation invisible as construction (dart DT-D parity).
decisions.resolution: super builds the superclass (walk-recorded first-base map), self/Self the enclosing type; the dangling leaf call is dropped. Unresolvable (no base) stays silent. Oracle mirrors via heritage prescan + ancestor climb. Gated by fixture swift/init-delegation + 3 mutants. CORRECTED 2026-09-25 (#941): the owner is the parent's `ownerName` when the parent is a MEMBER symbol and the parent's own `name` only when the parent IS the type (deinit/subscript/observer bodies, which have no symbol of their own). The old expression minted the enclosing symbol's own name (`instantiates constructor -> constructor`) wherever the owner was unresolvable, and the oracle's `consumed` flag only fired on the resolvable branch, so the truth side published the dangling `calls -> init`. SW-G's own words are now honored on both sides: unresolvable stays silent. Gated by fixture swift/error-recovery-nominal + 3 mutants.

decisions.node_type: prefix enum-case calls, Self enum calls
decisions.question: Second review: `.success(v)` implicit construction (prefix-expression callee, no identifier — silent) and `Self.failure(x)` (calls->failure) never built the enum, though both unambiguously construct it in enum context.
decisions.resolution: Candidates resolve against the ENCLOSING enum's cases (implicit) or Self+owner (explicit); non-enum owners and non-cases stay silent/calls. Oracle mirrors both shapes. Gated by fixture + 2 mutants.

decisions.question: Second review: `struct X: ~Copyable` error-recovers (the struct symbol itself is lost); deinit/willSet/didSet bodies source to the TYPE (no method symbol exists); nested types attribute owners exactly; `Optional.some(x)` stays a leaf call.
decisions.resolution: ~Copyable is a pinned-grammar boundary (both blind, corpora unaffected — same class as #expect/raw-strings). Observer/deinit bodies keep the type-fallback source (DARTD9 analog, consistent both sides). Nested nominals already exact. stdlib-enum qualified construction (Optional.some) stays out of scope: only in-file enum knowledge decides (cross-file named knowledge would need the companion).

decisions.node_type: call_expression recovered from a switch `case` pattern
decisions.question: #938: the pinned grammar does not reduce `case .websocket(let x):` — it recovers a call_expression whose callee navigation STARTS AT THE `case` KEYWORD (simple_identifier "case" + navigation_suffix), so the analyzer published a fabricated `calls -> websocket` for a pattern MATCH.
decisions.resolution: A pattern match is not a call and not construction: `isCasePatternRecovery` reads the callee navigation's first token (a reserved keyword, never text) and emits nothing, on BOTH sides (the oracle mirrors it). Measured: 3 analyzer-only rows at full extent (554 files of swift-nio), the lane's only unexplained-by-truth edges. Gated by fixture swift/case-pattern-recovery + mutant swift/case-pattern-keyword-call.

decisions.question: #939: the pinned grammar wraps a force unwrap in a `postfix_expression`, and the SCD1 climb listed only directly_assignable_expression / navigation_expression / navigation_suffix — so the inner navigation hit a wall on its first step, the LHS-span test never ran, and a WRITE was published as a read (`$0.platformSpecificStatus!.st_dev += 1`).
decisions.resolution: The climb traverses the unwrap wrapper in all three gates (handleSelfUse, handleBareUses' isWrite, handleMemberUses) and in the oracle's two mirrors, so the LHS-span rule decides on both sides. Both direction rows close at once: the nested write stops leaking a read AND the flat `x.a! = 1` pure write — which BOTH sides used to publish as a read — is gated. Gated by fixture swift/unwrap-write-gate + mutants swift/unwrap-inner-write-as-read / swift/unwrap-outer-write-as-read.

decisions.question: #940/#941: the pinned grammar cannot reduce `nonisolated(unsafe)`, so a whole class header lands in an ERROR node — no container symbol is minted and every member it owns is orphaned (no `contains`, no member inventory for bare reads, no owner for `self.init`). Bare-member reads went two-sidedly blind inside the file.
decisions.resolution: The recovery shape is read STRUCTURALLY, never from text: an ERROR whose first non-header child is the anonymous nominal keyword token (`class`/`struct`/`enum`/`extension`/`actor`) and whose own next named child is the type name (`user_type` for an extension, identifier otherwise). Declaration content before the keyword disqualifies the node — a nested declaration the recovery left as a SIBLING contributes its own keyword token (measured on `extension SocketAddressError { … struct UnknownHost … }`). The container, its heritage, its members and their owners all recover. Gated by fixture swift/error-recovery-nominal + mutants swift/error-recovery-no-container / -self-owner-target / -dangling-init-call.

decisions.question: #942: the enum-construction conversion removed "the first calls edge with this (source, leaf)" — a DIFFERENT call site's edge whenever two sites in one scope share a leaf name (`static var get: Endpoint { method(.get) }` beside `var path = Path.method(.get)`), and a record of a dangling call that no longer existed. The oracle mirrored the defect by splicing on target alone, so the loss was two-sidedly invisible.
decisions.resolution: The splice is SITE-precise: every call site increments a per-(source,leaf) count (the dedupe had already folded several sites into one relationship), the conversion retires exactly its own contribution, and the edge is dropped only when no non-construction site remains. The surviving edge is then re-lined onto a site that is STILL a call, per pool, never globally — two pools can share a source LINE. Gated by fixture swift/enum-construction-splice + mutants swift/enum-splice-first-edge / swift/enum-splice-no-conversion.

decisions.node_type: quoted identifiers, tuple positions, decorator payloads (name surface)
decisions.question: #924 (swift half): three shapes published a non-name as a name. (a) Swift's keyword-escape quoting was kept INSIDE the name (`` `continue` ``), while every corpus reference spells it bare, so such a name could never match a reference (29 symbols, 40 targets at full extent). (b) A tuple POSITION (`pair.0`, `_key.1`) was published as a member target (4 sites) — and after that target was dropped the edge's receiver leaked through a fallback (`queueCallbackPair.1(...)` -> `calls -> queueCallbackPair`, the lane's only remaining unexplained edge). (c) An attributed enum case (`@available(...) case x`) published the decorator PAYLOAD as the member's name and borrowed the decorator's line.
decisions.resolution: (a) exactly one surrounding backtick pair is stripped, at symbol creation, at every read site, and in the oracle. (b) a navigation suffix with no identifier child is not a name: the fallback that reached for the last simple_identifier child — the RECEIVER — is now blocked whenever a suffix was present (measured: exactly ONE site of that shape in 652 files, and it is a call through a tuple position). (c) the member name is the identifier after `case` (`modifiers` is metadata), and the range node is that identifier, so a decorated declaration's line is its own. Gated by fixture swift/attributed-enum-case + mutants swift/attributed-case-payload-name / -range-at-decorator; measured by the full-extent name census (652 files, 23,212 symbols, 78,747 targets, CLEAN).
